title: T-cell and cutaneous lymphoma
subtitle: Outcomes well behind B-cell disease — PTCL is consolidated with transplant in first remission, while mycosis fungoides is managed for decades. CD30 and blood involvement are the findings that change the plan
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin, pp.233–246 · NCCN Primary Cutaneous Lymphoma v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: Where T/NK neoplasms live
rows: PTCL-NOS · AITL and nodal TFH lymphomas · ALCL, ALK+ or ALK− (DUSP22 / TP63 / NOS) · EBV+ nodal T-cell
Extranodal NK/T, nasal type · enteropathy-associated (EATL) · monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal (MEITL) · hepatosplenic · subcutaneous panniculitis-like
Mycosis fungoides · primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs (lymphomatoid papulosis, C-ALCL) · primary cutaneous gamma/delta
Sezary syndrome · ATLL · T-PLL · T-LGL · aggressive NK-cell leukemia
blocks.footnote: WHO 5th edition 2024. Sezary syndrome sits in both the cutaneous and leukemic columns — that duality is the point: it is mycosis fungoides with blood involvement.

blocks.heading: PIT — peripheral T-cell lymphoma
blocks.footnote: One point each: age >60 · LDH > normal · ECOG 2–4 · marrow involvement. Gallamini, Blood 2004. Staging otherwise uses Ann Arbor. Compare these numbers with aggressive B-cell disease — even no-risk-factor PTCL does worse than high-risk DLBCL.

blocks.heading: MF/SS — ISCL/EORTC TNMB
rows: Patches/plaques <10% BSA · >10% BSA (T2a patch only, T2b plaque)
Clinically abnormal nodes by Dutch grade 1 / 2 / 3–4 (NCI LN 0–2 / 3 / 4)
≤5% of lymphocytes are Sezary cells, or <250/µL, and <15% CD4+CD26− or CD4+CD7−
>5% Sezary cells or >15% CD4+CD26−/CD7−, but not B2
>1,000/µL Sezary cells or >1,000 CD4+CD26−/CD7− cells/µL with a blood clone matching the skin
blocks.footnote: Stage IA T1 · IB T2 · IIA T1–2 N1–2 · IIB T3 · IIIA/B T4 with B0/B1 · IVA1 = Sezary syndrome (any T, B2) · IVA2 N3 · IVB M1. Olsen, Blood 2022.

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: Auto-HCT in first remission is the default for PTCL — the exception is ALCL with an ALK or DUSP22 rearrangement, which does well without it
Allogeneic transplant is potentially curative in advanced MF/SS — 1-yr and 3-yr OS 51% and 40%, PFS 42% and 33%, with acute and chronic GVHD 45% and 40%

† Sezary syndrome requires all three: erythroderma (T4, ≥80% BSA), B2 blood burden, and a T-cell clone in blood matching the skin. The older ISCL adjuncts — CD4:CD8 ≥10 and loss of CD7 or CD26 — no longer stand alone; modified ISCL/USCLC/EORTC criteria need the clone plus an absolute count. The handbook prints none of this, giving only stage IVA1

boxes: Subtype and CD30 drive the choice
PTCL-NOS, AITL, TFH: BV-CHP if CD30+, else
combos: DHAP · ESHAP · GDP · GVD · GemOx · ICE
IIB: local RT if limited, TSEBT if generalized,
Erythrodermic III, Sezary IV, and LCT
<5K/mm³: ECP + interferon or retinoids, TSEBT + ECP

blocks.heading: PTCL and NK/T regimens
rows: 30 mg/m² IV weekly ×6 — folic acid 1–1.25 mg daily from 7–10 d before until 30 d after, B12 1 mg IM q8–10 wk
Romidepsin 14 mg/m² over 4 h d1, 8, 15 q28d ×6 · belinostat 1,000 mg/m² over 30 min d1–5 q21d ×8
75 mg PO BID ×2 cycles, then 25 mg PO BID
Gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d · brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg d1 (max 180 mg) q21d ×16 if CD30+
Dexamethasone 40 mg + ifosfamide 1,000 + mesna + etoposide 67, all d1–3; carboplatin 200 d1
MTX 2,000 d1 · ifosfamide 1,500 + mesna + dexamethasone 40 mg + etoposide 100 d2–4 · pegaspargase 2,000 U/m² d7, hold until MTX <0.04. Leucovorin from 24 h. TMP-SMX DS BID Sat/Sun
blocks.footnote: CHOP/CHOEP/BV-CHP/DA-EPOCH dosing is not in this chapter — see the aggressive B-cell card. EATL: CHOP ×1 then IVE (ifosfamide 3,000 + etoposide 200 d1–3, epirubicin 50 d1) alternating with MTX 1,500 d22, q28d ×3, then auto-HCT.

blocks.heading: MF/SS therapies
rows: Topical corticosteroids · imiquimod · mechlorethamine (often compounded) · topical retinoids · local ISRT 8–12 Gy (24–30 Gy if unilesional) · TSEBT 12–36 Gy · PUVA for thicker plaques, NB-UVB for thinner
300 mg/m² PO daily — causes central hypothyroidism: follow free T4, not TSH; check lipids. Vorinostat 400 mg PO daily · IFN alfa-2a 3–6 MU daily or TIW · ECP
1 mg/kg IV d1, 8, 15, 22 then q28d — CCR4 antibody, best in Sezary/blood disease. Mogamulizumab-associated rash is delayed, median onset 119 days
Romidepsin 14 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d — QTc prolongation, replete Mg each infusion. Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg q3wk — thicker skin disease and LCT only; watch neuropathy
MTX 25 mg PO weekly (start 10–15, titrate); if higher doses are needed switch to pralatrexate 15 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d — half the PTCL dose; mucositis is dose-limiting
3 mg d1 then 10 mg SQ on alternating days, TIW, max 12 wk — stage III/T4 or Sezary only; CMV PCR q2–3 wk, Bactrim + acyclovir
200 mg IV q3wk — continue indefinitely; stopping can lose the response
blocks.footnote: Maximise skin-directed therapy and supportive care first — it lengthens time to the next systemic treatment. Check compatibility with TSEBT/phototherapy first, and recycle agents that previously worked.
